pinned_manifest_class_contract.rationale: The Phase 22 invocation inventory and the Phase 23 content-pattern text-surface manifest pin 578 of 2377 tracked files by whole-file digest, selected by content match rather than by path, so the blocked set is not enumerable from a path list. Every artefact a Stdlib or docs patch is made of - a justfile guard recipe, a CI workflow, a parity script, fixtures, and the documents that describe them - lands in one or both manifests, and a parity script cannot exercise both backend routes without naming them and thereby enrolling itself in the manifest that forbids new files. Patches 24.2i and 24.2n each lifted one instance. This registers the class: living surfaces are held by the content they must not lose instead of by bytes, and lane-owned appends are admitted while every closed-phase artefact stays exactly pinned.

relay_site_anchor.boundary_correction_is_not_a_defect: Patch 24.3c recorded 23258; this patch records 23176. Both over-restrict and neither under-protects, so no edit was ever wrongly admitted and there is no correctness bug in the merged patch. The safe regions nest - the region above 23258 is inside the region above 23209, which is inside the region above 23176 - so a lane scoping against any of the three is safe, merely more restricted than necessary. What was wrong was the label, not the number. Stdlib S1.10 edited at 23218, safe under all three, and confirmed it by measuring rather than by trusting the recorded value; that is how the mislabel was caught.
relay_site_anchor.highest_invocation_row_reason: NOT THE GENERAL TRIPWIRE - this names the RELAY ROW. 23258 is the live line of the single row this contract immunizes, and it is the highest of the 59 justfile invocation rows. Retained under this key because relay_site_anchor() requires it and because it is the most conservative of the available thresholds, but scope against highest_ordinary_invocation_row_line instead: this one over-restricts by 82 lines. Patch 24.3c recorded it as the highest invocation row, which is true, and it was then read as the highest row an edit must clear, which is a different claim.
relay_site_anchor.highest_ordinary_invocation_row_reason: THE TRIPWIRE. The highest live justfile invocation row that is NOT immunized, in recipe guard-stdlib-s1-collection-receivers. An edit below it in the file moves only the relay row at 23258, whose line is overwritten with the frozen pre_relay_line before the invocation manifest is hashed, so the one row that moves is projected away and no digest follows it. THAT MECHANISM, not the arithmetic, is why the region is safe - it survives a renumbering, whereas safe because 23218 is greater than 23176 does not. An edit ABOVE 23176 moves rows nothing projects and reaches the five further comparison sites plus two generated reviews listed below. Measured from phase22_opening.scan_invocations() at 7f83914d: 318 invocation rows, 59 in the justfile, descending 23258, 23176, 23175, 23168, 23164.
relay_site_anchor.line_projection_reason: KEEP the projection. It is why re-anchoring does not move invocation_manifest_digest for the relay row. It immunizes ONE row and no more - measured, f27c56c4 -> aaaf12d4 for a justfile edit above other invocations. An earlier reading of this code claimed the digest was immunized in general; that claim was wrong in scope and is recorded here so it is not repeated.
relay_site_anchor.rejected_selection_reason: the relay manifest guards the no-fallback guarantee under the Level-3 launch claim in docs/CRANELIFT_LAUNCH.md. Re-anchoring is lane work ONLY while it never admits an implicit_default invocation; admitting one would trade away that guarantee and is the operator's call, not this lane's. Asserted here so the condition cannot drift silently: the site keeps selection explicit_c and its --backend mir-to-c command verbatim.
relay_site_anchor.retired_reason: an absolute line number used as a proxy for a location. The relay site's recipe, command, compiler token and explicit route were all unchanged by Stdlib S1.10; only the coordinate moved, and that broke seven guards through this single assertion. A coordinate is not what the pin means - the site is identified by the recipe that owns it and the command it runs, and those are stable across exactly the edit that moved the line. This is a RE-ANCHOR, not a relaxation: the surviving conjuncts are strictly the ones that carry the guarantee.
relay_site_anchor.stored_coordinate_reading: DO NOT re-derive this boundary from stored registry values. phase22_explicit_c_migration.cross_lane_relay.authorized_site_manifest holds 8 justfile line values whose maximum is 23209, and NONE of the 8 matches any live invocation row - all eight have already drifted, because phase22_explicit_c_migration.py anchors on path, recipe and compiler_token with line deliberately excluded and never compares them to a live scan. They are display data, not a check. Taking their maximum as the boundary yields 23209, which is sound only by accident: it over-restricts against the live 23176 rather than under-protecting. The failure mode is reading a stored number as an enforced one, which is the same error this contract exists to correct, so it is named here rather than left to be rediscovered.
relay_site_anchor.unmeasured_coordinate: scripts/phase22_opening.py asserts row['line'] == 33 on tests/e2e_codegen_assertions.gst inside a falsifier self-test. No probe moved that file, so it is UNMEASURED rather than inert. It uses next(), so a shift raises StopIteration and the guard crashes instead of failing with a diagnostic that names the cause. tests/ is inside the Stdlib append scope, so it is reachable by the lane this patch serves.

relay_site_anchor.unretired_review_note: de-coordinate rather than regenerate. Both live under compiler/ and are Cranelift-owned, so a Stdlib patch can never regenerate them; regenerating leaves the coordinate embedded and re-arms the trap. pinned_manifest_class_contract.retired_census_spelling_reason: the census is forbidden as a gate item, not as a subject. The leading bullet is load-bearing: docs/CRANELIFT_LAUNCH.md quotes the old wording in prose to explain why it was replaced, and a check that forbade the words outright would forbid recording what was changed - which is how a correction loses its reasoning and gets re-proposed.

roadmap_projected_row.reason: Patch 24.2n projected TASK.md's digest onto the closed pre-amendment state but left its match_counts live, so the roadmap was only half unfrozen: editable only while never changing how many times it says MIR-to-C. Most Cranelift roadmap rows discuss backend parity, so that trap fires on the first ordinary row, and it had held only by luck. Project the whole content-derived row, which is the treatment every other registered living surface already receives. The path-derived fields - classification, owner, current_route, deprecation_action, removal_phase, falsifier - do not vary with content and are left alone.

structural_rules.reason: a status cannot be softened into prose and a rule row cannot vanish. Indifferent to any status changing, which is the progress the ledger exists to record. The minimum_units floor is load-bearing: 'every unit satisfies P' is vacuously true of zero units, so without it deleting every rule row would pass a rule written to catch exactly that.

no phase silently loses its exit gate. The floor was set at 6 against 8 live sections so the Phase 27 amendment, which removes one, would not trip the guard it landed under. That amendment has landed and 7 sections remain, each carrying an exit gate. The floor stays at 6 rather than being ratcheted to 7: the headroom is what lets an honest retirement happen without the guard having to be edited in the same patch, which is the pattern that turns a guard into a wall.

roadmap_living_surface.rationale: TASK.md is the Cranelift roadmap and every patch ticks a status row in it, so byte-pinning it forbids this lane from recording its own merged patches. Patches 24.2f-24.2h merged and the roadmap still reported them unstarted. This is the same freeze Patch 24.2i lifted for TASK_STDLIB.md; the landed roadmap record is held by content instead of by bytes.
